bug_description.normalized: In vulnerable commit `a26806801005c28115ae9e48bdcf3bbbc1bcd767`, GSUB subset closure constructs `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)` from font-backed Coverage data. The generic `hb_auto_t (T1 t1)` constructor copies that Coverage object by value into ctor-local `t1`, and `Coverage::Iter::init` then stores pointers into the copied coverage subtable. When the constructor returns, `iter.get_glyph()` reads through expired stack-backed coverage state, producing a poisoned glyph id that flows through `hb_set_t::page_for()` into `hb_vector_t::bfind()`, where MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at `else if (c > 0)`. Commit `2dde6c803a9e50c5bff74095187b0cb2e12eebdd` fixes the bug by deleting the catch-all by-value overload and allowing only pointer/reference `hb_auto_t` construction, so the iterator is initialized from the original Coverage object instead of a temporary copy.

source.description: The first vulnerability-relevant project statement on the crashing path dereferences the attacker-controlled GSUB `coverage` offset as `this+coverage` and uses that font-backed object to construct local iterator `iter`.
source.value_from: The fuzzed OpenType font reaches GSUB subset closure and supplies the `coverage` offset in the current `SingleSubstFormat1` subtable; `this+coverage` resolves that table view from attacker-controlled font bytes.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer reports the crash when binary search branches on comparison result `c`, which was computed from a page-map key derived from the poisoned glyph id.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable helper takes the Coverage object by value and initializes `Coverage::Iter` from ctor-local copy `t1`. Because the nested iterator stores pointers into the passed-in coverage object, `iter` ends up retaining pointers into stack state that expires when the constructor returns.

parser_admitted.description: On the witnessed subset path, `close_over_gsub` is true, so `_populate_gids_to_retain` calls `_gsub_closure` and dispatches attacker-controlled GSUB subtables.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan attributes the origin to stack allocation of local `iter` in this loop. The following steps close why that stack object becomes poisoned: its internal coverage pointers are initialized from ctor-local copy `t1` instead of the original font-backed table.

coarse_trace.summary: Subset planning keeps GSUB closure enabled and calls `_gsub_closure` on the attacker-controlled face, reaching `SingleSubstFormat1::closure`.
Constructing `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` from `this+coverage` routes through the vulnerable by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor, so the iterator retains pointers into ctor-local copied coverage state.
A poisoned glyph id from the stale iterator is converted into `page_map_t key`, and `hb_vector_t::bfind()` later branches on comparison result `c` derived from that key.

fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled GSUB `coverage` offset is resolved as `this+coverage` and immediately used to construct local iterator `iter`.
The generic one-argument constructor copies the Coverage object by value into ctor-local `t1` and initializes `Coverage::Iter` from that temporary. This accidental copy is the root cause.

fine_trace.code: switch (format) { case 1: u.format1.init (c_.u.format1); return; case 2: u.format2.init (c_.u.format2); return; }
fine_trace.note: Iterator initialization reads the copied Coverage format and forwards the chosen copied subtable into the nested iterator. Both nested init routines store `c = &c_`, so `iter` keeps a pointer into ctor-local `t1` instead of the original table.
After the constructor returns, `iter.get_glyph()` dereferences nested iterator state that still points into expired ctor-local coverage storage and materializes poisoned `glyph_id`.
The poisoned glyph id is consumed by the retained-glyph membership test and forwarded into `hb_set_t::page_for(glyph_id)`.
The set lookup derives page-map search key `key.major` from poisoned glyph id `g`. MSan's secondary stack identifies this store as the point where the uninitialized value is written into `key`.
The poisoned page-map key is passed unchanged into the binary search over the set's page map.
Binary search compares `x.major` from the poisoned key against the current page-map entry and produces tainted comparison result `c`.
MSan sink. The binary-search branch consumes tainted comparison result `c` and reports use-of-uninitialized-value at this control-flow use.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MSan attributes the origin to the `iter` stack slot in `SingleSubstFormat1::closure`; the fine trace closes why that slot becomes poisoned by showing `hb_auto_t (T1 t1)` initializing it from constructor-local Coverage copy `t1`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Commit `2dde6c803a9e50c5bff74095187b0cb2e12eebdd` removes the generic by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor and replaces it with pointer/reference overloads only, preventing `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` from copying Coverage into ctor-local `t1`.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` match workspace checkout `a26806801005c28115ae9e48bdcf3bbbc1bcd767`, and repository history shows `2dde6c803a9e50c5bff74095187b0cb2e12eebdd` as the direct one-commit fix for this exact constructor bug.

format.name: OpenType font
format.contract: An OpenType font that reaches subset planning with GSUB closure enabled and dispatches a `SingleSubstFormat1` subtable, so `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)` is constructed from font-backed Coverage data on the crashing path.
